fields.headline: STATE DEPARTMENT BUYS FACE CHECKS
fields.deck: The contract could reach $6.5 million, but records do not name the products.

frames.mediaQuery: Paravision facial recognition deepfake detection product

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a contract worth up to $6.5 million, according to federal procurement records. The department made the award on September 23 and initially obligated $1.3 million. The contract is priced as a firm fixed price and can run through September 22, 2031.

The department ran the buy as a simplified acquisition restricted to small businesses and received only one offer. Federal records describe the work as "digital detection/identity assurance," but they do not name the Paravision products the department purchased. That description matches technology Paravision sells to protect digital identity systems against manipulated and AI-generated faces. The company's line includes facial recognition, passive liveness detection and deepfake detection. Its deepfake tool checks still images and video frames for digital manipulation, and the company has extended it to spot fully synthetic faces made with diffusion models and generative adversarial networks.

The public contract record does not show whether the award covers any of those products. A separate $24,717 purchase order dated April 30, for a "purchase card for software license," does not identify the software and does not show whether it was a test, pilot or precursor to the September contract.

Source: Biometric Update, October 17, 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

PATROLS THE GULF
WITHOUT A CREW

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH / SEASATS

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel ingress, in U.S. waters.

Why: Each vessel is roughly 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds, and two people can launch and recover it from a boat ramp or a pickup truck.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Fleet deployed in support of U.S. maritime border security operations, per Seasats. Lightfish vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026.

Seasats says a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels is now deployed to support U.S. maritime border security. The fleet launched from the Texas coast into the Gulf of America to keep watch on illegal maritime activity. The move expands work Seasats has already done supporting Operation River Wall on the southern border, and it sits inside an existing autonomous surveillance effort led by the Pentagon's homeland defense and Americas security office.

The vessels run on solar power and can stay on station for multiple months. Each one has a modular payload bay, and past missions have carried infrared and electro-optical cameras, signals payloads and sonar. Seasats says it holds more than $100 million in U.S. government contracts.

Seasats CEO Mike Flanigan said the Gulf is too large to monitor with crewed hulls alone, and that a fleet of the vessels can provide continuous coverage of an area previously seen only in snapshots. Assistant Secretary of War Mark R Ditlevson said Seasats is one of many industry partners helping secure the nation's maritime domain.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, 2 Oct 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE GEAR IN AFRICA
fields.deck: Soldiers would receive tested systems within 180 days under the new partnership.

stories.caption:
U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) has teamed with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to trial new systems on the continent and get them into Soldiers' hands within 180 days.

The command's first accelerated capability event (ACE) is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It will concentrate on counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, aimed at shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. The event follows a three-phase model of submission and preparation, Soldier-led demonstrations, and follow-on operational evaluation. Its five capability categories cover an integrated fly-away kit plus four areas: sUAS detection, kinetic defeat, nonkinetic defeat and passive protection.

SETAF-AF plans a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027 in Tan-Tan, then an operational assessment in April and May during African Lion 2027. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner, and winners will plug into the Army's Integrated Battle Command System-Maneuver for C-UAS command and control. G-TEAD placed a team with SETAF-AF in summer 2026. G-TEAD director Col. Christopher Hill said that ASCCs "always had priorities" and capability gaps, but had never held acquisition authority or research, development, test and evaluation dollars.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Pfc. Marley Kamara

Microchip Technology acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and HARDSIL process technology to its space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge, its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard ran Drone Crucible 26.3 at Camp Blanding, Sept. 26 to Oct. 2, linking drone, Tactical Assault Kit and video data into a shared operational picture.

Source: MilCityUSA ICYMI, week of Oct. 5, 2026. Original sources: Microchip Technology, Oct. 9, 2026; Lockheed Martin, Oct. 9, 2026; Florida National Guard report, Oct. 6, 2026.
